What Is the 25% Rule for Roofing?

The 25% rule is a rule of thumb that a roof with more than about a quarter of its area damaged is usually better replaced than patched; it is not a statewide mandate for houses. Under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, re-covering a detached one- or two-family home is ordinary maintenance, and on other buildings a permit is required when repairs exceed 25% of the roof area within 12 months.

sections.heading: How to Choose a Roofing Contractor and Roofing Materials in Bloomfield

runs.v: How to Tell If a Roofer Is Lying

Ask for the New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor registration and proof of insurance, and get every scope in writing: under the NJ Contractors' Registration Act, home improvement contracts over $500 must be written, and the homeowner can cancel within three business days. Red flags include pressure to sign on the spot, large cash deposits, and vague line items. A Google review history helps, but compare written estimates with transparent pricing.

An experienced roofing company should explain the fastening pattern, ventilation math, and flashing plan. Whether a crew calls itself an experienced team or an expert team, ask how its experienced roofers deliver precise installation and reliable workmanship, because quality materials give long-lasting protection only when installed correctly. If siding installation or other exterior work is planned, schedule it after the new roof so the step flashing and trim tie in behind the siding.

faqs.q: Do you need a permit for asphalt shingle roofing in Bloomfield, NJ?

faqs.q: What is the difference between 3-tab and architectural shingles?

runs.v: Architectural shingles bond multiple fiberglass-mat layers into a dimensional profile that lasts about 30 years and rates up to 130 mph with the manufacturer 6-nail pattern; 3-tab shingles are a single flat layer that lasts about 20 years and rates near 60 mph, per InterNACHI, ARMA, and manufacturer guidance. Modern architectural shingles handle Northeast winters and heavy nor'easters well.

runs.v: Architectural shingles last about 30 years and 3-tab about 20, per InterNACHI, and actual life varies up to 40% with climate, installation, and attic ventilation, per the NRCA.
